summary: Independent replay of every decision the uxdec handoffs mark as applied, on a fresh production build (ux:build of the integrated working tree, base 9f68f49), on Chromium, desktop WebKit and the iPhone 13 emulation, plus a regression sweep of every e2e/routes.ts route. Verdicts: 25 verified, 1 partly (D22), 5 unchanged as required (D3, D14 outcome, D29, D30, D31), 0 not, 0 regressed. Six observations recorded as new findings; none is a regression of this branch: two are pre-existing target sizes, the others are by-design limits worth one owner line each.

decisions.status: owner decision 2026-10-05 (option C: A and B)
decisions.notes: Clock: on the first 'Up next' screen the ring read '0 of about 30 min' before and after 6 s of real time under ?fast=1 (2 session minutes); every 'Up next' screen shows 'The clock waits until you press Start.'; after Start the ring moved to '1 of about 30 min' within 2 session minutes; on the next 'Up next' screen and on the break offer the reading was held again. Break: skipping Reaction Time (from inside the part), Matrix & Series and Spatial brought 'Time for a break?' before 'Up next: Working Memory' with the new text ('about half-way ... The clock waits until you press Start on the next part.'), no '30 minutes'; taking it and resuming led to Working Memory with no second offer; no offer after Working Memory or Quantitative Reasoning. Budgets: with four parts skipped the Quantitative Reasoning screen said 'About 5 minutes' (the finding had 'About 14 min'). Two whole ?fast=1 sessions per engine, one without skips and one skipping Spatial, read 'About N minutes' as RT 3, MAT 5, SPA 5, WM 5, QR 5, PS 4 in both, so a skip made no later part longer; both journeys completed (49 to 51 s of real time) with the one break before Working Memory. Measured, not a defect: the ring's total stays 'about 30 min' (the planned target) after skips. Owner line (run.json open issue, seen here): the offer still comes before Working Memory when every earlier part was skipped.

After one answer in Matrix & Series and a reload, the ready screen shows 'Continue your unfinished session' (primary, 44 px) beside a plain 'Begin' and the line 'Your session from today at HH:MM was not finished. Continue it to go on from the start of Matrix & Series and keep what you have done so far. Begin starts a new session instead.' (Title Case part name, D25); Continue leads to 'Up next: Matrix & Series'. Axe: 0 serious. The sitting model (no practice adjustment between a session and its continuation) is a unit and golden matter (engine-retest.json); the server variant offers nothing, as resume.json says.

Continue with the slider where it started: the autosave's response tuple holds confidence_pct null (e.g. ['i:series:1.3.0:...', 0, '1', 0, 150, null]) and flags.confidence_untouched_n is 1; the next item with the slider moved to 70 records 70 and the counter stays 1. Same in all three engines.

In the Quantitative part: '1,500' is refused with 'Write thousands without a comma (1500) and decimals with a point (1.5).' on whole-number, fraction and decimal items; '3,5' is accepted as an answer on fraction items (Chromium, iPhone: 'Enter a fraction such as 3/8, or a whole number.') and decimal items (WebKit: 'Enter a number; decimals are fine, such as 12.5.'), and on a whole-number item gets the unchanged whole-number note; no hint says 'integer'. The bank twin and the server reader are unit and db-test matters (quant-entry.json, integrate.json).

Coding block running, nine keys measured: 320 x 568 two rows, keys 53.4 x 50 px; 390 x 664 two rows, 67.4 px; 412 x 840 (the Pixel 7 width) two rows, 71.8 px; 430 x 932 one row, 40.7 px (as before); no sideways overflow; block height 345 px folded (table top to last key), 291 px in one row. Same in Chromium, WebKit and iPhone. The timed response path was not re-timed on a device (render.json says so too).

Please do not use a calculator or an AI chatbot. Screen readers, zoom and other accessibility settings are fine to use.'; nothing tells screen-reader users to stop using one. Quantitative 'Up next' screen: 'Scratch paper and a pencil are fine; please do not use a calculator or an AI chatbot.'; the old 'Keep paper and a calculator out of reach' is gone. issues.detail: Targets under the 44 px phone comfort size, all over WCAG 2.5.8's 24 px except one: the standalone links 'Privacy and terms' (24 px, on 22 states per engine), 'Privacy and terms (opens in a new tab)' (24 px, every session screen), 'Back' on the privacy page (24 px), 'Read the full privacy notice and terms' on the gate (24 px); the checkbox inputs of the gate (26 px), the honour code (26 px) and 'Add my new session to the ...' on ready-continue (26 px) inside their 44 px label rows; the notes page's 'Show all topics' and 'Why this line?' (40 px); and the notes card's 'Make notes for your AI (opens in a new tab)' link on results-saved and share-card-dark, 18 px tall at 1280 px (38 px at 200% text, 42 px at 320 px). app.css gives standalone links min-height 24 px on purpose. Listed per state in each summary.json under metrics.<state>.smallTargets.
item-spatial-no-webgl: 'THREE.WebGLRenderer: Error creating WebGL context.' logged once by three.js in each engine; the route stubs WebGL out to show the skip panel.

new_findings.summary: A browser that only kept notes settings on the notes page (no session consent record yet) gets no 'Earlier results and notes on this device' row and so no 'Notes for your AI' link on the welcome, although D22 says the link shows when kept notes exist. By design in funnel.json (nothing is read before the gate: the row needs an adult consent record of the session flow, and the notes page keeps its own 18+ tick). With a consent record present the link shows, even when the notes and the session sit under different identifiers (then 'See my results' is withheld and the ready screen asks which).
new_findings.suggestion: An owner line: either accept (and say so in D22's record) or let the notes page's 18+ tick count as the adult record for the welcome row.

new_findings.summary: The notes card's 'Make notes for your AI (opens in a new tab)' link on the results page after the save is 18 px tall at 1280 px (a link alone in its paragraph: WCAG 2.5.8 asks 24 px unless the target is in a line of text), 38 px at 200% text and 42 px at 320 px. RevealCard.svelte is unchanged on this branch; wave 2's VER-02 looked at the privacy links, not this one.
new_findings.suggestion: Give the link the .hb-standalone-link treatment (min-height 24 px) or a 44 px row like the welcome's notes link.

new_findings.summary: The break is offered before Working Memory even when Reaction Time, Matrix & Series and Spatial were all skipped (zero active minutes): the literal half-way rule, as run.json's open issue says. Seen in the D5 replay in all three engines.
new_findings.suggestion: Owner choice: keep the literal rule or offer the break only after a part has run.

new_findings.summary: At script pace (gate and honour code passed in well under a second) the device screen still shows 'Checking your screen' for about 850 to 870 ms while the measurement that started on the gate finishes; at a person's pace (1.5 s on the honour screen) Continue is enabled within 2 ms and the text never shows. Expected from the handoff ('the screen waits for what is left of it, once'); recorded so the number is on file.

In headless desktop WebKit, after a later question's region ('Question 2') takes the focus, one Tab lands on nothing (document body) instead of the first option; Chromium reaches the option. Likely WebKit's Tab-to-controls setting (the screen package noted a related WebKit Tab quirk after a mouse click); the region itself is focused as designed in every engine.
new_findings.suggestion: Worth a check in real Safari with 'Press Tab to highlight each item' on; no change proposed from an emulation alone.

new_findings.summary: At 200% text on a 390 px phone no part of the chart is in the first screen (the h1, lead line and save pointer take it); at 100% text 66% of the chart is. reveal.json lists this as open; recorded with the measurement.
new_findings.suggestion: Shorter Finished lead lines on phones (integrate.json's open request) would help most.
